calls.head: The Canucks can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is the league’s best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.7 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 26th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s power play created 8.6 expected goals per 60 in 6:30 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 9.7, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: Quality over quantity for the Oilers
calls.body: The Oilers make their shots count, and the Canucks are one of the league’s worst at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Oilers to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Oilers’ average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Edmonton 9th for shot quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Vancouver 31st for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s average shot had a 6.0% chance of going in, against their usual 6.6%.

calls.head: Active D against forward-led
calls.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, at the active D end; the Canucks are one of the league’s worst, at the forward-led end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Canucks’.

calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Edmonton had 34% and Vancouver 29%. Coming in, Edmonton was at 38% and Vancouver at 32%.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 75% chance, but Vancouver had other ideas.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver a 25% chance, and Vancouver proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Vancouver won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Edmonton wins 83. Vancouver won anyway.

surprises.head: A rough night for T. Jarry
surprises.body: T. Jarry allowed 6 goals on shots worth 2.3 expected goals, 3.7 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 90 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Vancouver hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 41, against their usual 100 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton tried a different line
surprises.body: K. Kapanen, L. Draisaitl, V. Podkolzin played 12:14 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Edmonton’s usual lines.

story.head: A hat trick for Bouchard
paras: Paul Cotter scored twice, opening the scoring midway through the first. Evan Bouchard scored three. Three times the Oilers answered a Canucks lead. Cotter won it 1:59 into overtime.

The Oilers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Oilers win about four in five. The Oilers tried a line they hadn’t used before: Kasperi Kapanen, Leon Draisaitl and Vasily Podkolzin, and it had a hand in both of their goals.

items.text: Whether the Oilers keep that line together in Vancouver on Thursday.
One of the preview’s three calls held.
